summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule to update its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to reflect statutory changes enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The 2021 amendments broadened FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all federal civilian service — including temporary and intermittent work — toward the required 12 months of qualifying service, and also clarified that annual and sick leave earned under non-Title 5 authorities can be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. The 2021 amendments also excluded all Veterans Health Administration employees covered under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from Title 5 FMLA coverage, shifting their coverage to a separate VA-administered framework. The 2023 amendment further expanded eligibility by allowing honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward the 12-month service requirement, though Coast Guard and Public Health Service commissioned corps service does not qualify. Because paid parental leave eligibility depends on FMLA eligibility, these changes also affect which federal employees can access paid parental leave; the rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026.
